name: Antique Classical

description.short: The Greek and Roman architecture of antiquity, in which the orders were first codified and the proportional method invented.
description.long:
Everything downstream in the classical stream is a reading of this material. Greek building gave the West a system of proportion derived from a module rather than from absolute measure, and a set of orders that graduate character from robust to delicate. Roman building gave it the arch, the vault, the dome, and a bureaucratic capacity to standardize and export the whole apparatus across three continents.

What matters for a design system is that these are the only two bodies of ancient architecture the West has ever possessed complete enough to reverse-engineer. Every revival since the fifteenth century has worked from surviving Roman fabric and, after the 1750s, from measured Greek fabric — which is why the revivals differ so sharply in the accuracy of what they reproduce.

defining_characteristics: Proportional derivation from a module rather than absolute dimension
The orders as a graduated system of architectural character
Trabeated Greek construction and arcuated Roman construction as two distinct structural logics
Temple and domus as the two type-diagrams the West kept returning to
